ei.title: 2번: How Tall Buildings Affect Wind Speed
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.

questions.passage: Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was (A)[stronger / weaker] near tall buildings. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also (B)[decrease / increase] wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the (C)[narrow / wide] spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) stronger=더 센 / weaker=더 약한 (B) increase=증가시키다 / decrease=감소시키다 (C) narrow=좁은 / wide=넓은
det.analysis:
① weaker—decrease—narrow: (A)(B) 높은 건물 근처에서 바람은 '더 약한' 게 아니라 '더 센(stronger)', 여러 건물은 풍속을 '감소'가 아니라 '증가(increase)'
② stronger—increase—narrow: 높은 건물 근처 바람이 더 셈 + 여러 건물이 풍속을 증가 + 좁은 틈 ←정답
③ weaker—increase—wide: (A)(C) 문맥과 반대
④ stronger—decrease—wide: (B)(C) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 높은 건물 근처 바람 stronger(더 셈), 여러 건물은 풍속 increase(증가), 통로 효과는 narrow(좁은) 틈

det.korean: (A) higher=더 높은 / lower=더 낮은 (B) strong=센 / weak=약한 (C) faster=더 빠른 / slower=더 느린

det.korean: (A) tall=높은 / short=낮은 (B) high=높이 / low=낮게 (C) narrower=더 좁은 / wider=더 넓은

③ (A) 공간 (B) 공간: (B) 지구 밖에서 일하는 것은 '우주'

det.tip: space의 다의어: 건물 사이의 좁은 공간/틈 vs 지구 밖 우주

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to happen or take place, especially without being planned"

det.korean: vanish=사라지다 / remain=남다 / occur=발생하다 / expand=팽창하다
det.analysis:
① vanish: 사라지다 — 일어나는 것과 반대
② remain: 남다 — 의미 다름
③ occur: 계획 없이 일어나거나 발생하다 — 정의와 일치 ←정답
④ expand: 팽창하다 — 의미 다름
det.tip: to happen or take place = 발생하다(occur)

questions.passage: This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water __________ (flow) in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: flow(동사: 흐르다) → flowing (명사 water를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사)
det.analysis: 명사 water(물) 바로 뒤에서 '흐르고 있는'이라는 뜻으로 물을 꾸며 주려면 동사 flow에 -ing를 붙인 현재분사 flowing으로 써요. water (that is) flowing in a river = 강에서 흐르고 있는 물처럼, 이렇게 앞의 명사를 꾸미는 분사예요.
det.tip: 명사(water)를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사 → water flowing in a river

questions.passage: This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind __________ (blow) through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: blow(동사: 불다) → blows (주어 the wind가 3인칭 단수라서 현재형에 -s)
det.analysis: 이 글은 늘 일어나는 일반적 사실을 현재시제로 설명하고 있어요. when(~할 때)이 이끄는 절의 주어가 the wind(바람)로 3인칭 단수이므로, 현재시제 동사에는 -s를 붙여 blows로 써야 해요. 동사원형 blow는 3인칭 단수 주어와 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: 3인칭 단수 주어(the wind) + 현재시제 → 동사에 -s → blows

questions.passage: Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't __________. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: stop the wind=바람을 멈추다 / go through it=그것을 통과하다 / change into rain=비로 변하다 / block the sun=해를 가리다
det.analysis:
① stop the wind: 바람이 바람을 멈춘다? 어색함
② go through it: 센 바람이 높은 건물을 치면 건물을 '통과할' 수 없어서, 대신 위·아래·옆으로 감 ←정답
③ change into rain: 비로 변한다? 문맥 무관
④ block the sun: 해를 가린다? 문맥 무관
det.tip: hit a building + Instead, go up/down/around → 건물을 통과할(go through it) 수 없음

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: rises into the clouds=구름 속으로 오르다 / spins around the roof=지붕 주위를 돌다 / fades near the top=꼭대기 근처에서 약해지다 / shoots down to the ground=땅으로 빠르게 내리꽂히다
det.analysis:
① rises into the clouds: 구름으로 오른다? 거리 높이의 센 바람과 연결 안 됨
② spins around the roof: 지붕을 돈다? 문맥 무관
③ fades near the top: 꼭대기에서 약해진다? '거리에서 세다'는 흐름과 반대
④ shoots down to the ground: 바람이 땅으로 빠르게 내리꽂혀 거리 높이에서 세다 ←정답
det.tip: The wind that ___ is strong at street level → 땅으로 내리꽂히는(shoots down to the ground) 바람
